summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sir Vivian Richards Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as England posted 187/10 (60.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 306/10 (130.6 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Collapse: Lost 10 Wickets for 97 Runs, which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, KAJ Roach delivered a masterclass for West Indies (6 Runs & 8 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (West Indies 49%) and allowing West Indies to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, England faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. West Indies's bowling unit, bolstered by Moeen Ali (64 Runs & 3 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing West Indies won by 10 wickets in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: West Indies's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While England produced fighting phases, West Indies won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
